# AI Coding Guide for RoboBlast

- Engine: Godot 4 (GDScript, 3D). Entry scenes: main gameplay in [main.tscn](../main.tscn); player prefab lives in [player/player.tscn](../player/player.tscn).
- Run/debug: open the project in Godot and press F5. Required input actions are listed in README; `Player` auto-registers missing ones at runtime.
- Controls: move WASD, mouse to aim, Space jump, LMB shoot, RMB aim, Tab swap weapons (bullet ↔ grenade), Escape pause (handled by demo overlay).
- Workspace purpose: the Godot game scene is a demo bed for developing the `GDInsight` addon under [addons/GDInsight](../addons/GDInsight); use it to playtest interactions while iterating on the plugin.
- Core architecture: `Player` ([player/player.gd](../player/player.gd)) is a `CharacterBody3D` with embedded `CameraController`, `GrenadeLauncher`, `CharacterSkin`, UI nodes, and signals (`weapon_switched`). Movement is camera-oriented, smoothed via `_last_strong_direction`, with gravity/air-boost handling in `_physics_process`.
- Camera: `CameraController` ([player/camera_controller.gd](../player/camera_controller.gd)) manages two pivots (third-person vs over-shoulder), raycasts for aim target/collider, and keeps height in sync with `_ground_height` from the player.
- Weapons: default bullets use [player/bullet.gd](../player/bullet.gd) (Area3D, distance-based lifetime, ignores shooter, damages `damageables`). Grenades use `GrenadeLauncher` ([player/grenade_launcher.gd](../player/grenade_launcher.gd)) to compute arcs, snap to `targeteables` via `ShapeCast3D`, draw the trajectory mesh, and instantiate [player/grenade.gd](../player/grenade.gd) which bounces, then explodes using an `Area3D` and calls `damage` on `damageables`.
- Damage contract: any actor that can be hurt implements `damage(impact_point, force)` (e.g., [enemies/bee_bot.gd](../enemies/bee_bot.gd), [enemies/beetle_bot.gd](../enemies/beetle_bot.gd), [box/box.gd](../box/box.gd), `Player`). Bullets/grenades rely on this method and group membership `damageables` to apply effects; grenades ignore objects of type `Player` when exploding.
- Enemy patterns: `BeeBot` hovers, tracks player when inside detection area, fires bullets on a timer, and drops coins + smoke puff on defeat. `BeetleBot` uses `NavigationAgent3D` to chase/ram, triggers attack animation on collision, and also drops coins/puff on defeat.
- Interactables: `jumping_pad` applies an upward impulse plus tweened squash/stretch; `box` spawns coins and swaps to a destroyed-box scene on damage; both rely on the shared `damage` or `body_entered` interactions.
- Animation/FX: `CharacterSkin` ([player/character_skin.gd](../player/character_skin.gd)) drives the animation tree state machine and emits `stepped` for footstep sounds. Bullets scale down over time via an exported `Curve`. Grenade launcher draws its path mesh each physics frame while visible.
- UI & flow: demo overlay ([demo_page/demo_page.gd](../demo_page/demo_page.gd)) pauses the tree, shows keyboard/joypad instructions, and restores prior mouse mode. Weapon UI and coin HUD are children of `Player` (see `%CoinsContainer`, `%AimRecticle`).
- Input map expectations (see README): `move_left/right/up/down`, `camera_left/right/up/down`, `jump`, `attack`, `aim`, `swap_weapons`, `pause`. The player registers defaults if absent, but exporting a build should define them in project settings.
- Scene/groups conventions: enemies and breakables are tagged `damageables`; grenade snapping looks for `targeteables`. When adding new actors, set the group membership to participate in combat logic.
- Physics usage: `Player` uses `move_and_slide`; bullets move in `_process` with manual position updates; grenades use `move_and_collide` with bounce decay; enemies are `RigidBody3D` with impulses for hit reactions.
- Assets: coins live under [player/coin](../player/coin), explosion VFX under [player/explosion_visuals](../player/explosion_visuals), smoke puff under [enemies/smoke_puff](../enemies/smoke_puff). Keep resource paths consistent when instantiating.
- Extending: prefer adding new weapons by following the bullet/grenade split—cooldowns and weapon toggling are in `Player._physics_process`, and UI listens to `weapon_switched`. New damageable targets should implement `damage` and join relevant groups.
- Performance cautions: trajectory mesh in `GrenadeLauncher` rebuilds every physics frame while visible—toggle `visible` off when not aiming. Bullets compute lifetime from speed/distance; set `velocity` before adding to the tree.
- When copying the character to another project, also copy `player` and `shared` folders (shaders) as noted in README; ensure input actions are present or allow the runtime registrar to add them.
- No automated tests; manual playtest via Godot editor is the validation loop.
- Addon: `GDInsight` plugin lives in [addons/GDInsight](../addons/GDInsight). Plugin entry is [gdinsight.gd](../addons/GDInsight/gdinsight.gd) (EditorPlugin scaffold). `api.gd` defines `API` Node with `HTTPRequest` GET/POST helpers and example calls to GitHub API and a PHP endpoint—replace URLs with your backend. Enable plugin via Project Settings → Plugins to autoload/test.
- Addon goals (see [docs/TODOs.md](../addons/GDInsight/docs/TODOs.md)): build a graph-based SQL visualizer using `GraphEdit`, with nodes per table and edges for relationships; sync via HTTP to a PHP backend; plan CRUD and graph-to-SQL translation. Use the demo scene to validate visualization overlays (heatmaps, paths, labels) against gameplay data.
- Network testing: `API.fetch_data(url)` → GET with basic JSON parse logging; `API.send_data(url, dict)` → POST JSON. Hook plugin UI to these helpers; remember Godot’s HTTP requests must run from a scene tree node (e.g., autoload or editor plugin singleton) and require internet permissions in export presets if shipping.
- GDInsight TODO quicklist (see [docs/TODOs.md](../addons/GDInsight/docs/TODOs.md) for detail):
	- GraphEdit UI: create nodes for SQL tables, connect edges for relationships, save/load graph.
	- Data sync: HTTPRequest ↔ PHP backend ↔ SQL; decide cache vs on-demand; emit signals on changes.
	- CRUD: tables and records (create/read/update/delete) plus graph-to-SQL translation layer.
	- Visualization hooks: heatmaps/paths/labels to overlay gameplay analytics inside the demo scene.
